title: POC scoping: benchmark harness integration - Nimbus Health
summary: Scoping call to align on POC success criteria and benchmarks. Discussed workload sizing (qps, concurrency, token lengths), streaming vs non-streaming test approaches, harness integration (Locust/JMeter/WebSocket), dataset and eval scripts, and a 3-week timeline for baseline, optimization, and report. Agreed next steps and owners to share benchmark plan, harness guides, and sample traffic/eval datasets.
next_steps: Schedule kickoff + baseline test week (Leah) - target 2025-06-12
Customer to provide sample traffic trace & 200 eval prompts (Nate) - by 2025-06-13
Redwood to run hosted baseline and share raw results (Ravi) - by 2025-06-18
action_items: Leah - send benchmark-plan.xlsx and pricing sheet (link) by 2025-06-11
Ravi - share benchmark harness integration guide and sample Locust/JMeter and WebSocket scripts by 2025-06-12
Nate - export a 48hr traffic trace and provide 200 canonical eval prompts by 2025-06-13
Priya - grant temporary read-only access to a small subset of request logs (if possible) by 2025-06-13
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-10 15:00 PT | Duration: ~48 minutes
Attendees: Leah Park (Redwood AE), Ravi Singh (Redwood SE), Nate Moore (Nimbus CTO), Priya Shah (ML Eng), Lina Gomez (Platform)
---
[00:00] Leah: hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros, i'm leah from redwood, ravi is our se, and we wanted to go through the poc scoping and specifically the benchmark/harness integration piece.
[00:12] Nate: thanks leah, yeah we want to validate throughput and latency for our chat and batch scoring workloads, and understand hosted vs dedicated cost tradeoffs.
[00:20] Ravi: cool. to start, can you run through your expected traffic patterns and success criteria? that'll help us pick tests.
[00:28] Priya: sure. our main workload is a patient-facing chat; typical session length is 8-12 messages, average prompt ~450 tokens, responses average ~220 tokens. at peak we see about 15 concurrent chats which translates to roughly 20 rps for generation calls during certain hours. p50/p95 latency expectations are pretty strict: p50 < 250ms first token, p95 < 800ms for non-streamed full response. p99 we'd like under 1.5s if possible.
[01:05] Lina: for batch scoring we have nightly jobs that submit ~10k records, but latency is not as critical there, throughput and cost are.
[01:15] Ravi: okay that's helpful. streaming vs non-streaming: chat needs streaming to deliver first token fast; batch scoring can be non-streaming HTTP. we'll design two harnesses.
[01:28] Leah: we'll plan baseline runs on hosted first to get apples-to-apples versus your current vendor, then run targeted tests on Dedicated instances to show cost/perf curves.
[01:36] Nate: one ask: our security team needs audit logs and KMS details before we do dedicated. is that something you can share?
[01:43] Leah: yes; i'll send SOC2 + KMS integration docs and a short packet on Private vs Dedicated controls. link in the follow-up.
[01:50] Ravi: on the harness side, what do you currently use for load testing? locust, jmeter, homegrown?
[01:56] Priya: primarily Locust for HTTP; we have a small websocket harness but it's brittle. we'd prefer Redwood's examples for streaming tests.
[02:04] Ravi: we have sample Locust scripts for non-streaming and a websocket/async python harness for streaming. i'll share both. important note: streaming measurement is tricky — you want to measure time-to-first-token and throughput of incremental chunks; our harness reports both.
[02:18] Leah: also we'll want to warm the kv cache to avoid cold-start artifacts — we'll include instructions for warmup patterns.
[02:25] Nate: good call. what's the recommended warmup?
[02:28] Ravi: for chat-style models, run a ramp of simulated sessions over 10-15 minutes to populate caches and kernel JITs. for batch, do a small warm batch run. we'll provide concrete scripts.
[02:38] Priya: sounds good. for success criteria, we care about two things: 1) latency SLOs for interactive chat (as listed), and 2) cost per 1M tokens below an internal target — we gave a rough target to procurement but will confirm.
[02:52] Leah: perfect. we'll produce a benchmark plan that includes metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, time-to-first-token (streaming), tokens/sec, token cost estimate, and accuracy/regression on a 200-prompt eval set.
[03:04] Lina: on accuracy/regression, we need to ensure outputs don't degrade vs our baseline; how do you do regression testing?
[03:10] Ravi: we run an eval harness that scores model outputs on your reference prompts using a mix of automated metrics (BLEU/ROUGE/custom) and manual review for critical cases. for the poc we'll run automated scoring and flag failures for manual review. we can accept your scoring script if you have one.
[03:24] Nate: we have a small eval script that scores for relevance and safety heuristics; i'll send that.
[03:29] Priya: about dataset size for eval — 200 prompts is our current plan, representative across modalities.
[03:35] Leah: timeline-wise we were thinking: week 0 - kickoff and data + scripts exchange; week 1 - hosted baseline runs; week 2 - tuning and dedicated runs if applicable; week 3 - final report and decision. does that align?
[03:47] Nate: yes that matches our 3-week internal approval window.
[03:51] Ravi: a few technical notes for integration: 1) for streaming tests we emulate the websocket protocol and measure TTF token per chunk; 2) for throughput we recommend steady-state runs of 10 minutes at target qps and a 30-minute soak at peak QPS to catch degradation; 3) for cost estimates we record token counts and model instance hours.
[04:14] Priya: for our peak, we'll target two profiles: steady 20 rps (concurrency ~15) and a spike test to 60 rps for 5 minutes to see graceful degradation.
[04:24] Ravi: good — we'll define the spike profile in the plan. also, if you want to test KV cache effectiveness we'll run identical prompts to show token savings with prefix caching.
[04:34] Nate: i like that. can you run both open models and our current vendor's model for comparison?
[04:39] Leah: yes, we'll run the models we have in the catalog and try to mimic your vendor's config where possible — model size, quantization, and sequence length will be matched.
[04:48] Lina: procurement will ask for a data retention and encryption statement; please include that in your packet.
[04:54] Leah: yes included. we'll attach a short compliance FAQ.
[05:00] Ravi: on infra: if we do Dedicated tests we'll need a capacity reservation; we can start with small reserved nodes for the benchmark week to ensure stability.
[05:09] Nate: does Redwood provide a trial for Dedicated or do we need a contract first?
[05:13] Leah: we can provision short-term dedicated capacity for POC under an MSA addendum for benchmarks; i'll outline options in the follow-up.
[05:22] Priya: about the harness integration: are there specific headers or tracing hooks to send? we instrument with x-request-id and traceparent.
[05:29] Ravi: yes, include x-request-id, traceparent, and an x-customer-env header so we can splice logs in our observability dashboard. we'll also supply a short guide for exporting trace context.
[05:40] Nate: what about streaming chunk sizes — we see differences in real world; do you control chunk granularity?
[05:45] Ravi: chunking is model + runtime dependent; we can control flush sizes at the runtime level for experiments and will measure chunk latency.
[05:52] Leah: i'll recap actions at the end but quick note: please don't share sensitive PHI in the eval prompts; pseudonymize where possible.
[06:00] Priya: understood.
--- mid call chatter and deeper technicals ---
[20:00] Ravi: (screen share) here's the locust script example. key points: for non-streaming batch we make a POST /generate and measure request completion; for streaming we open websocket and measure first message time and final message time.
[20:30] Priya: how do you capture p99 for streaming where some users stay connected longer?
[20:36] Ravi: we cap session duration for the test and focus on generation time; long-polling clients are out of scope for this benchmark.
[22:12] Nate: any gotchas around JIT warmup and kernel selection? we saw noisy results the first run before warm caches.
[22:20] Ravi: yes very common; we recommend discarding first 1-2 minutes of metrics and running a warmup phase. we'll provide a recommended runbook.
[30:05] Leah: ok outline of deliverables: benchmark-plan.xlsx, harness scripts (locust + websocket), warmup/runbook, security packet, and a short dedicated provisioning options doc.
[30:18] Nate: good. for scoring we'll want the raw result set and aggregated metrics (latency histograms, token counts) so our team can reproduce.
[30:27] Ravi: we'll provide raw logs and summary dashboards and a CSV export.
[36:40] Priya: one more question: if we find a regression in quality after quantization, what's the remediation path?
[36:48] Ravi: we can iterate on quantization profile, try different bit widths, or fall back to float models for problematic prompts. part of the POC is to chart quality vs cost for those tradeoffs.
[37:02] Leah: ok wrapping up. next steps and action items we'll put in the follow-up. any final questions?
[37:10] Nate: none from me, this is great.
[37:12] Priya: no, thanks.
[37:15] Lina: all good.
[37:20] Leah: thanks everyone, we'll send the packet. talk soon.
[37:24] (call ends)
notes: Shared artifacts: benchmark-plan.xlsx (will be attached in follow-up), harness examples (locust + websocket), security packet (SOC2 + KMS notes)
Customer to pseudonymize PHI before sending prompts
